questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Causes of low MCV and MCHC (microcytic hypochromic anaemia):

options.label: A
options.explanation: The commonest cause: inadequate iron limits haem synthesis, giving small, pale red cells with low ferritin.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hepcidin traps iron in macrophages; usually normocytic but can become microcytic hypochromic, with normal or high ferritin.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Haemolysis gives a normocytic (or macrocytic, from reticulocytosis) picture, not microcytosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Acute haemorrhage produces normocytic normochromic anaemia; microcytosis appears only after chronic loss depletes iron stores.

questions.pearl: Microcytic causes - TAILS: Thalassaemia, Anaemia of chronic disease, Iron deficiency, Lead poisoning, Sideroblastic anaemia.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Formed elements derived from megakaryocyte cytoplasm; normal count 150-400 x10^9/L.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Leucocytes are formed elements of blood, normal count 4-11 x10^9/L.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Erythrocytes are the most numerous formed element, about 45% of blood volume (haematocrit).

options.label: D
options.explanation: The fluid component, about 55% of blood volume, containing water, proteins, electrolytes and clotting factors.

questions.pearl: Blood is about 55% plasma and 45% formed elements; serum is plasma minus clotting factors.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Variation in cell and nuclear size and shape, with hyperchromatic nuclei, is a hallmark of dysplasia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Mild to moderate dysplasia may regress if the stimulus is removed (e.g. stopping smoking); full-thickness change (carcinoma in situ) is less likely to.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Normal orderly maturation and orientation of cells is lost (architectural anarchy).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Mitoses are increased and may appear at abnormal levels of the epithelium, not decreased.

questions.pearl: Dysplasia involving the full epithelial thickness without basement membrane breach is carcinoma in situ.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cisterns are dilated parts of the subarachnoid space (e.g. cisterna magna) where CSF pools.

options.label: B
options.explanation: CSF circulates in the subarachnoid space between arachnoid and pia mater.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Major cerebral vessels run in the subarachnoid space, which is why aneurysm rupture causes subarachnoid haemorrhage.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Spinal nerve roots traverse the subarachnoid space before piercing the dura; the cauda equina floats in the lumbar cistern.

questions.pearl: Berry aneurysm rupture bleeds into the subarachnoid space: thunderclap headache, xanthochromic CSF.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: The Mantoux reaction is a classic delayed (48-72 h) T-cell mediated response.

options.label: B
options.explanation: SLE is immune-complex mediated, i.e. type III hypersensitivity.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Nickel or poison ivy dermatitis is a delayed T-cell mediated reaction.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Beta-cell destruction is driven by autoreactive CD8 and CD4 T cells, a type IV mechanism.

questions.pearl: Type IV is the only cell-mediated (T cell) type and cannot be transferred by serum.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Acute gout classically affects a single joint, often the first metatarsophalangeal joint (podagra).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Must be excluded in any hot swollen single joint; aspirate before antibiotics.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Typically an asymmetrical oligoarthritis of the lower limbs, not a monoarthritis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A symmetrical small-joint polyarthritis of hands and feet.

questions.pearl: Hot swollen single joint: septic arthritis until proven otherwise - aspirate for Gram stain, culture and crystals.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.text: Occur most commonly between 6 months and 5 years of age
options.explanation: Typical age range is 6 months to 5 years, with a peak at 14-18 months.

options.label: B
options.text: Occur several times in a day
options.explanation: A simple febrile seizure occurs once in 24 hours; recurrence within 24 hours makes it complex.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Simple febrile seizures last less than 15 minutes; longer ones are complex.

options.label: D
options.explanation: There is no residual neurological deficit; a postictal focal deficit (Todd paresis) indicates a complex seizure.

questions.pearl: Simple febrile seizure: generalised, under 15 min, once in 24 h, no deficit, no meningitis; family history in about half.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: 10 mL of 10% calcium gluconate stabilises the cardiac membrane within minutes; it does not lower potassium.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Nebulised beta-2 agonist shifts potassium into cells via Na/K-ATPase.

options.label: C
options.explanation: ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone and raise potassium; they should be stopped.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Removes potassium from the body in refractory hyperkalaemia, especially with renal failure.

questions.pearl: Hyperkalaemia sequence: stabilise (calcium), shift (insulin-glucose, salbutamol), remove (resins, diuretics, dialysis).

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Massive vasodilatation and capillary leak cause hypotension, not hypertension.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Mast cell mediators (histamine, leukotrienes) cause bronchospasm and wheeze.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Upper airway angio-oedema causes stridor and can be rapidly fatal.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Sweating, flushing, urticaria and clammy skin are common accompaniments.

questions.pearl: First-line for anaphylaxis: IM adrenaline 0.5 mg (0.5 mL of 1:1000) into the anterolateral thigh, repeat after 5 min.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Cardinal symptoms of type 1 diabetes mellitus:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Glycosuria causes osmotic diuresis once blood glucose exceeds the renal threshold (about 10 mmol/L).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Thirst follows the fluid loss of osmotic diuresis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Insulin deficiency causes catabolism and weight loss, not gain.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cells are starved of glucose despite hyperglycaemia, driving increased appetite.

questions.pearl: Classic triad of type 1 DM: polyuria, polydipsia, weight loss; ketoacidosis may be the first presentation.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Glomerular inflammation lets red cells leak, giving cola-coloured urine and red cell casts.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Reduced GFR raises urea and creatinine.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Salt and water retention from reduced GFR causes hypertension and oedema.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Sodium is retained with water, so serum sodium is usually normal; hypernatraemia is not a feature.

questions.pearl: Nephritic syndrome: haematuria, oliguria, hypertension, oedema, mild proteinuria (under 3.5 g/day).

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Haemolytic uraemic syndrome (HUS) is characterised by:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Not a feature; leukoerythroblastic picture suggests marrow infiltration, and HUS is a thrombotic microangiopathy, not vasculitis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Red cells are sheared in damaged microvessels, producing schistocytes and raised LDH.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Arthritis is not part of HUS; the triad is MAHA, thrombocytopenia and acute kidney injury.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Acute kidney injury with raised urea (uraemia) is the defining renal component.

questions.pearl: Typical HUS follows Shiga-toxin E. coli O157:H7 diarrhoea in children; avoid antibiotics as they may worsen it.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: TSH-receptor antibodies stimulate diffuse thyroid enlargement, often with a bruit.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Graves' ophthalmopathy causes exophthalmos (proptosis), not enophthalmos.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Not part of the triad; high fever suggests thyroid storm or another cause.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Thyroid dermopathy, with exophthalmos and goitre, completes the classic triad.

questions.pearl: Graves' triad: diffuse goitre with thyrotoxicosis, ophthalmopathy, pretibial myxoedema; plus thyroid acropachy.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Chronic malabsorption (e.g. coeliac disease) causes growth failure.

options.label: B
options.explanation: 45,XO girls have short stature, the most consistent feature, treated with growth hormone.

options.label: C
options.explanation: 47,XXY causes tall stature with eunuchoid proportions.

options.label: D
options.explanation: GH excess before epiphyseal fusion causes tall stature.

questions.pearl: Tall stature: familial, Marfan, Klinefelter, homocystinuria, gigantism, precocious puberty (early), hyperthyroidism.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery
questions.stem: Clinical features of gastric outlet obstruction:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Loss of HCl in vomitus causes hypochloraemic hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Vomiting of undigested, non-bile-stained food is characteristic.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Sodium is lost in vomitus and urine, giving hyponatraemia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The obstructed, distended stomach causes early fullness and a succussion splash.

questions.pearl: GOO gives paradoxical aciduria: the kidney retains Na+ and K+ in exchange for H+ despite alkalosis.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Rapid infusion of cold stored blood lowers core temperature; use blood warmers.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Potassium leaks from stored red cells into the bag.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Citrate anticoagulant chelates calcium, causing hypocalcaemia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Dilution of platelets and clotting factors causes dilutional coagulopathy.

questions.pearl: Lethal triad in trauma: hypothermia, acidosis, coagulopathy.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Gap junctions in intercalated discs allow the myocardium to act as a functional syncytium.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Mature skeletal fibres are electrically independent, each activated by its own motor neurone.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Electrical synapses between neurones are formed by gap junctions (connexons).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Spermatozoa are free cells and have no gap junctions.

questions.pearl: Gap junctions are formed by connexin proteins and also couple visceral smooth muscle cells.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Examples of congenital cyanotic heart disease:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Left-to-right shunt, acyanotic unless Eisenmenger syndrome develops.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The commonest cyanotic congenital heart disease after infancy; right-to-left shunt across the VSD.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Left-to-right shunt, acyanotic; reversal gives differential cyanosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: No forward pulmonary flow; survival depends on a duct, causing cyanosis.

questions.pearl: Cyanotic 5 Ts: Tetralogy, Transposition, Truncus arteriosus, Tricuspid atresia, TAPVR.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pellagra causes diarrhoea, not constipation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Photosensitive dermatitis on exposed skin, e.g. Casal necklace.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Neuropsychiatric change from confusion to dementia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pellagra gives a raw red glossitis; geographic tongue is a benign idiopathic condition.

questions.pearl: Pellagra 4 Ds: dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia, death; seen with maize diets, isoniazid and carcinoid syndrome.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Obstructs the distal CBD, giving progressive painless jaundice.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Worms can migrate into the CBD and cause biliary obstruction, common in endemic areas.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Compresses the distal CBD; palpable gallbladder (Courvoisier's law).

options.label: D
options.explanation: CBD stones are the commonest cause of obstructive jaundice, often fluctuating and painful.

questions.pearl: Courvoisier's law: painless jaundice with a palpable gallbladder is unlikely to be due to stones.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.text: It is accumulation of excessive fluid in the peritoneal cavity
options.explanation: This is the definition; about 1500 mL is needed for shifting dullness.

options.label: B
options.text: Chronic liver disease is a common cause
options.explanation: Cirrhosis with portal hypertension causes about 75-80% of ascites.

options.label: C
options.text: Ascitic protein >25 g/L indicates transudative ascites
options.explanation: Protein above 25 g/L traditionally indicates an exudate; SAAG is now preferred.

options.label: D
options.text: Hepatocellular carcinoma causes low SAAG ascites
options.explanation: HCC (usually on cirrhosis, or with portal vein invasion) gives high SAAG ascites; peritoneal carcinomatosis gives low SAAG.

questions.pearl: SAAG of 11 g/L or more means portal hypertension (cirrhosis, heart failure, Budd-Chiari); under 11 suggests TB, peritoneal malignancy, pancreatitis.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Raised in ovarian choriocarcinoma and some dysgerminomas, so it is a recognised germ-cell tumour marker.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The main marker for epithelial ovarian cancer, used in the risk of malignancy index.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Not an ovarian marker as such; it may rise in mucinous tumours but mainly suggests a GI primary.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Raised in yolk sac (endodermal sinus) tumours.

questions.pearl: Germ-cell markers: AFP (yolk sac), hCG (choriocarcinoma), LDH (dysgerminoma); inhibin for granulosa cell tumours.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Mitral leaflets are held wide open by high atrial pressure and close forcefully.

options.label: B
options.explanation: This mid-diastolic murmur occurs in severe aortic regurgitation, not mitral stenosis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The mid-diastolic murmur is a low-pitched rumble with presystolic accentuation.

options.label: D
options.text: Best heard with the bell of the stethoscope
options.explanation: Low-frequency sounds are best heard with the bell at the apex, patient in left lateral position.

questions.pearl: Severity of MS: the closer the opening snap to S2 and the longer the murmur, the more severe.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Commonly used drugs in heart failure:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Venodilator that reduces preload; used in acute pulmonary oedema.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Loop diuretic for symptomatic relief of congestion.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Traditionally used in acute pulmonary oedema to reduce anxiety and preload, though now used cautiously.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Calcium channel blockers give no benefit in HFrEF; amlodipine is neutral and not a heart failure drug.

questions.pearl: Mortality-reducing HFrEF drugs: ACE inhibitor/ARNI, beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2 inhibitor.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Unopposed lateral rectus and superior oblique pull the eye down and out: divergent squint.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Levator palpebrae superioris is supplied by the oculomotor nerve.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Loss of parasympathetic fibres to the sphincter pupillae; typical of compressive (surgical) palsy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Synechiae are adhesions from uveitis, unrelated to third nerve palsy.

questions.pearl: Painful third nerve palsy with a dilated pupil: posterior communicating artery aneurysm until proven otherwise.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Infectious mononucleosis, hepatitis and CMV cause absolute lymphocytosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Protozoal infection causing a mononucleosis-like lymphocytosis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: ITP is an isolated thrombocytopenia; the white count is normal.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Clonal B-lymphocyte proliferation, often over 5 x10^9/L, with smudge cells.

questions.pearl: Also pertussis: marked lymphocytosis in a child with whooping cough.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cholesteatoma can erode the facial canal: an intratemporal complication.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Mastoiditis and subperiosteal abscess are extracranial complications.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Labyrinthine fistula (often lateral semicircular canal) leads to labyrinthitis, an intratemporal complication.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Brain abscess is intracranial.

questions.pearl: Intracranial complications of CSOM: extradural, subdural and brain abscess, meningitis, lateral sinus thrombophlebitis, otitic hydrocephalus.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Mediators that increase capillary permeability in acute inflammation:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Causes endothelial contraction in venules, producing the immediate transient leak.

options.label: B
options.explanation: PDGF is a growth factor for fibroblast and smooth muscle proliferation in repair, not a permeability mediator.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Increases vascular permeability and causes pain.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Angiotensin II is a vasoconstrictor, not an inflammatory permeability mediator.

questions.pearl: Permeability mediators: histamine, serotonin, bradykinin, C3a/C5a, leukotrienes C4/D4/E4, PAF, substance P.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Signs of good positioning in breastfeeding:

options.label: A
options.text: Head and body in a straight line
options.explanation: One of the four signs of good positioning.

options.label: B
options.explanation: This is a sign of good attachment, not positioning.

options.label: C
options.explanation: One of the four signs of good positioning.

options.label: D
options.explanation: This is a sign of good attachment, not positioning.

questions.pearl: Positioning: straight, close, facing breast (nose to nipple), fully supported. Attachment: chin on breast, mouth wide, lower lip out, more areola above.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: According to IMCI, general danger signs (severe pneumonia) in a child aged 2 months to 5 years are:

options.label: A
options.explanation: One of the four IMCI general danger signs.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A sign of pneumonia, but not one of the general danger signs.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Indicates severe disease but is not listed among the general danger signs.

options.label: D
options.explanation: One of the four IMCI general danger signs.

questions.pearl: IMCI general danger signs: unable to drink or breastfeed, vomits everything, convulsions, lethargic or unconscious.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Mainstay to suppress inflammation, e.g. prednisolone acetate 1% drops.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Atropine or cyclopentolate relieves ciliary spasm pain and prevents posterior synechiae.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Used as an adjunct for pain and inflammation.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Indicated for severe, bilateral or steroid-drop-resistant uveitis.

questions.pearl: Anterior uveitis: circumcorneal congestion, small irregular pupil, keratic precipitates; dilate to prevent synechiae.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Locally invasive jaw tumour that rarely metastasises.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Locally destructive (rodent ulcer) but almost never metastasises.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A squamous cell carcinoma in a chronic scar; behaves as a true malignancy and can metastasise once it crosses the scar.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Highly malignant with early lymphatic and haematogenous spread.

questions.pearl: Locally malignant tumours: BCC, ameloblastoma, giant cell tumour, desmoid tumour, dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Deep apnoeic coma is a precondition for testing rather than a brainstem sign; simple unconsciousness occurs in many reversible states.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Fixed pupils unresponsive to light indicate loss of midbrain function.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Spinal reflexes, including deep tendon reflexes, may persist after brainstem death.

options.label: D
options.text: Loss of respiratory response to CO2 in the absence of hypoxia
options.explanation: The apnoea test: no breathing despite PaCO2 above 6.0 kPa confirms medullary death.

questions.pearl: Brainstem tests: pupillary, corneal, vestibulo-ocular, gag/cough, motor response in cranial territory, apnoea test.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Immediate management of acute severe asthma:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Give high-flow oxygen to keep SpO2 94-98%; controlled low-concentration oxygen is for COPD with CO2 retention.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Nebulised salbutamol 5 mg, repeated or continuous, with ipratropium.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Prednisolone 40-50 mg orally or IV hydrocortisone, reduces relapse and mortality.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Patients are often dehydrated from tachypnoea and poor intake; IV fluids and potassium monitoring are needed.

questions.pearl: Life-threatening asthma: PEF under 33%, SpO2 under 92%, silent chest, normal or rising PaCO2.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Upper airway obstruction (tumour, trauma, bilateral cord palsy) is the classic indication.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Elective tracheostomy is done after major head, neck or oral surgery to secure the airway.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Allows tracheobronchial toilet in patients unable to cough, e.g. after head injury.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Reduces dead space by about 50% and permits prolonged ventilation.

questions.pearl: Tracheostomy reduces anatomical dead space by about 50%; the ideal site is the 2nd-3rd tracheal rings.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Drugs contraindicated or best avoided in hepatic failure:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hepatotoxic and causes cholestasis; avoid or use with close LFT monitoring.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Directly hepatotoxic, causing fibrosis and cirrhosis; contraindicated in liver disease.

options.label: C
options.explanation: NSAIDs precipitate GI bleeding and hepatorenal failure, and diclofenac itself can cause hepatitis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Erythromycin estolate causes cholestatic hepatitis and the drug is hepatically cleared.

questions.pearl: In liver failure also avoid opioids and sedatives, which can precipitate hepatic encephalopathy.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Structures that are part of the visual pathway:

options.label: A
options.explanation: The thalamic relay where optic tract fibres synapse before the optic radiation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The midbrain carries the pupillary reflex pathway (pretectal nucleus), not the main visual pathway to the cortex.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The primary visual cortex (area 17) lies around the calcarine sulcus.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The fourth nerve is motor to the superior oblique, not part of the visual pathway.

questions.pearl: Visual pathway: retina, optic nerve, chiasma, optic tract, LGB, optic radiation, visual cortex.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: The intraocular lens can decentre or dislocate, especially with zonular weakness.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Postoperative inflammation is common; treated with topical steroids.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Retained cortex or nucleus causes inflammation and raised pressure.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Risk rises after cataract surgery, particularly with posterior capsule rupture.

questions.pearl: Commonest late complication of cataract surgery: posterior capsular opacification, treated with Nd:YAG capsulotomy.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: The eyes converge, not diverge, for near vision.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Contraction relaxes the zonules, letting the lens become more convex.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The pupil constricts (miosis) to increase depth of focus.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The lens thickens and its anterior surface becomes more curved.

questions.pearl: Near triad: convergence, accommodation, miosis. Argyll Robertson pupil accommodates but does not react to light.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: It is dislodgement of a clot, as blood pressure rises, that causes reactionary bleeding.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Relaxation of vasospasm, not spasm itself, causes bleeding within 24 hours.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A slipped ligature is a classic cause of reactionary haemorrhage.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A rise in BP after recovery from anaesthesia and shock causes reactionary bleeding.

questions.pearl: Primary: at operation; reactionary: within 24 h; secondary: 7-14 days, due to infection.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Severe myalgia and arthralgia give dengue its name of break-bone fever.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Abrupt high fever, often biphasic (saddle-back), lasting 2-7 days.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pain behind the eyes, worse on eye movement, is characteristic.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Not a typical feature; persistent vomiting and abdominal pain are the warning signs that matter.

questions.pearl: Dengue warning signs: abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, mucosal bleed, lethargy, liver enlargement, rising haematocrit with falling platelets.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Thyroxine is secreted by the thyroid gland.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Secreted by thyrotrophs of the anterior pituitary.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Secreted by corticotrophs of the anterior pituitary, derived from POMC.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cortisol is secreted by the zona fasciculata of the adrenal cortex.

questions.pearl: Anterior pituitary: GH, TSH, ACTH, prolactin, FSH, LH. Posterior pituitary releases ADH and oxytocin made in the hypothalamus.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Painful swallowing from floor-of-mouth cellulitis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Inflammation involving the pterygoid muscles limits mouth opening.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Spread to the larynx causes airway obstruction, the main cause of death.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Bilateral cellulitis of the submandibular, sublingual and submental spaces.

questions.pearl: Ludwig's angina usually arises from the 2nd or 3rd lower molar; brawny swelling with the tongue pushed up and back.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: The hepatic portal vein carries blood from gut capillaries to hepatic sinusoids.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Glomerular capillaries drain via efferent arterioles into peritubular capillaries, an arterial portal system.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Gastric veins drain into the hepatic portal system, but the stomach itself has no portal circulation.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The hypophyseal portal system carries hypothalamic releasing hormones to the anterior pituitary.

questions.pearl: A portal system is two capillary beds in series: hepatic, hypophyseal and renal.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Recurrent or failed trial without catheter after acute retention is an indication.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Back-pressure damage to the kidneys is an absolute indication.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Upper tract dilatation indicates obstruction needing relief.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A small residual volume alone is not an indication; large residuals (over about 200-300 mL) are.

questions.pearl: Absolute indications for TURP: retention, renal impairment, recurrent UTI, bladder stones, recurrent haematuria, hydronephrosis.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Transmitted sexually, parenterally and vertically.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Treponema pallidum is spread sexually and transplacentally.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Neisseria gonorrhoeae causes urethritis and cervicitis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Caused by HPV types 6 and 11 (condylomata acuminata).

questions.pearl: STIs often coexist: test anyone with one STI for HIV and syphilis.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Healing of periurethral inflammation causes fibrous stricture, typically bulbar.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Ascending infection causes salpingitis, tubal blockage and infertility.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Spread along the male genital tract involves the prostate.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Ascending infection via the vas deferens in men under 35.

questions.pearl: Disseminated gonococcal infection: arthritis, tenosynovitis and pustular skin lesions.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Colorectal carcinoma causes rectal bleeding with change in bowel habit.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Causes steatorrhoea from exocrine failure, not bloody diarrhoea.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Diverticular bleeding and diverticulitis can give bloody stools.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Causes frequent loose stools from rapid transit, without blood.

questions.pearl: Bloody diarrhoea: shigella, campylobacter, E. coli O157, amoebiasis, UC, Crohn's colitis, ischaemic colitis, colorectal cancer.

questions.subject: Gynecology
questions.stem: Causes of vaginal discharge with itching:

options.label: A
options.explanation: May cause vulval itching but not vaginal discharge.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Presents with painful vesicles and ulcers rather than an itchy discharge.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Frothy greenish-yellow discharge with itching and strawberry cervix.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Thick curdy white discharge with intense vulval itching.

questions.pearl: Bacterial vaginosis: thin grey fishy discharge, usually without itching; clue cells and positive whiff test.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Rodent ulcer is the eroding form of BCC.

options.label: B
options.text: Is the most common type of skin cancer
options.explanation: BCC is the commonest skin malignancy, mainly on sun-exposed face.

options.label: C
options.text: Presents as a shiny, pearly skin nodule
options.explanation: Pearly rolled edge with telangiectasia is characteristic.

options.label: D
options.text: Skin biopsy is needed for diagnosis
options.explanation: Histology confirms the diagnosis; excision biopsy is often curative.

questions.pearl: BCC: rolled pearly edge, telangiectasia, above a line from the angle of mouth to ear lobe; almost never metastasises.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pure uric acid stones are radiolucent on plain X-ray but visible on CT.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Xanthine stones are radiolucent.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Calcium oxalate stones are the commonest and are radio-opaque.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Calcium phosphate and struvite (staghorn) stones are radio-opaque.

questions.pearl: Cystine stones are faintly radio-opaque; non-contrast CT KUB detects nearly all stones.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Blood pressure falls as volume loss progresses; hypotension appears after about 30% loss.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The earliest compensatory sign from sympathetic drive.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Renal hypoperfusion causes prerenal failure and acute tubular necrosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cerebral hypoperfusion causes dizziness and light-headedness.

questions.pearl: Class III haemorrhage (30-40% loss): pulse over 120, falling BP, confusion, urine 5-15 mL/h.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Marjolin's ulcer, a slow-growing SCC, arises in long-standing burn scars.

options.label: B
options.explanation: BCC is very rarely reported in scars; the classic scar malignancy is SCC.

options.label: C
options.explanation: TCC arises from urothelium, not skin.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Not a recognised typical complication of burn scars.

questions.pearl: Marjolin's ulcer is painless and slow because scars lack nerves and lymphatics; nodes involved once it breaches the scar.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pancarditis, especially valvulitis of the mitral valve, is a major criterion.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Migratory polyarthritis of large joints is a major criterion; monoarthritis also counts in moderate/high-risk populations (2015 Jones).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Not a Jones criterion; erythema marginatum is.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A prolonged PR interval is a minor criterion.

questions.pearl: Major Jones criteria - JONES: Joints, O (carditis), Nodules, Erythema marginatum, Sydenham chorea; plus evidence of recent streptococcal infection.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Generalised gaseous distension of small and large bowel.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Effortless effluent vomiting from accumulated gut fluid.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Bowel sounds are absent or reduced (silent abdomen).

options.label: D
options.explanation: There is absolute constipation, with no passage of flatus.

questions.pearl: Common causes of paralytic ileus: postoperative, hypokalaemia, peritonitis, retroperitoneal haematoma.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: 15-20 g of fast-acting carbohydrate in the conscious patient.

options.label: B
options.text: Glucose gel applied to buccal mucosa
options.explanation: Useful if the patient is drowsy but can swallow, or in children.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Not a treatment for hypoglycaemia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Not a treatment for hypoglycaemia.

questions.pearl: Unconscious hypoglycaemia: IV 10% or 20% dextrose, or IM glucagon 1 mg if no IV access.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Sabin oral polio vaccine is live attenuated; IPV (Salk) is inactivated.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Measles, mumps and rubella components are all live attenuated.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Standard hepatitis A vaccines are formalin-inactivated.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Oral live attenuated vaccine given in infancy.

questions.pearl: Live vaccines are avoided in pregnancy and immunosuppression; other live viral vaccines include varicella, yellow fever.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Features of some dehydration following diarrhoea include:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Restless or irritable is a sign of some dehydration; lethargy indicates severe.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Dry mouth and tongue indicate some dehydration.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Sunken eyes are a sign of some dehydration.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Absent tears appear in some dehydration.

questions.pearl: Some dehydration (plan B): ORS 75 mL/kg over 4 hours.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Vaccines included in the EPI schedule in Bangladesh:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Bangladesh EPI gives MR (measles-rubella) at 9 and 15 months; mumps vaccine is not included.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Included in the pentavalent vaccine (DPT-HepB-Hib) at 6, 10 and 14 weeks.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Not part of the routine Bangladesh EPI schedule.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Not in the routine Bangladesh EPI schedule.

questions.pearl: Bangladesh EPI: BCG, pentavalent, OPV, IPV (fractional), PCV, MR, plus TT/Td for women.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: The main inhibitory transmitter in the brain, opening chloride channels.

options.label: B
options.explanation: An excitatory neuropeptide in pain pathways.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The main excitatory transmitter of the CNS.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Mainly inhibitory, e.g. inhibition of prolactin secretion and in the basal ganglia via D2 receptors.

questions.pearl: Glycine is the main inhibitory transmitter of the spinal cord; strychnine blocks its receptor.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.text: The electrical event precedes the mechanical event
options.explanation: Depolarisation triggers excitation-contraction coupling, so the QRS precedes ventricular systole.

options.label: B
options.text: T wave is due to repolarisation of the ventricle
options.explanation: Ventricular repolarisation produces the T wave.

options.label: C
options.text: P wave is due to atrial depolarisation
options.explanation: The P wave represents atrial depolarisation; atrial repolarisation is hidden in QRS.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Sinus arrhythmia: heart rate rises in inspiration via vagal withdrawal.

questions.pearl: Normal PR interval 0.12-0.20 s; QRS under 0.12 s; each small square is 0.04 s at 25 mm/s.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.explanation: Stored in blue cylinders as a liquid under pressure, in equilibrium with its vapour.

options.label: B
options.text: Is a gas above a temperature of 36 degrees C
options.explanation: Its critical temperature is 36.5 degrees C; above this it cannot be liquefied.

options.label: C
options.text: Cylinders should have a filling ratio of 0.65-0.75
options.explanation: The filling ratio is kept at 0.67 in temperate and 0.75 or lower in tropical climates.

options.label: D
options.text: Content in a cylinder is reflected by its pressure gauge
options.explanation: Pressure stays constant until the liquid is used up; content must be judged by weighing.

questions.pearl: Nitrous oxide: MAC 104%, good analgesic, causes diffusion hypoxia - give 100% oxygen at the end.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.text: There is fixation of the stapes
options.explanation: Otospongiotic bone at the fissula ante fenestram fixes the stapes footplate.

options.label: B
options.text: It occurs mostly in younger females
options.explanation: Usually presents at 20-30 years, more in women, and worsens in pregnancy.

options.label: C
options.text: Hearing loss is marked but speech is good
options.explanation: Conductive loss with soft, well-modulated speech; patients also hear better in noise (paracusis Willisii).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Bilateral in about 70% of cases.

questions.pearl: Otosclerosis: Carhart's notch at 2 kHz, Schwartze sign, As-type tympanogram; treatment is stapedotomy.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Tuberculoid leprosy gives well-formed epithelioid granulomas.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Tertiary syphilis produces gummas, a granulomatous lesion.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Causes non-caseating granulomas in liver, spleen and bone marrow.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Rickettsial infection causes vasculitis, not granulomas.

questions.pearl: Caseating granuloma: TB. Non-caseating: sarcoidosis, Crohn's, berylliosis, cat-scratch disease (stellate).

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Features of systemic inflammatory response syndrome:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Temperature above 38 or below 36 degrees C is a SIRS criterion.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Or PaCO2 below 32 mmHg.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Tachycardia is a SIRS criterion.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Or below 4 x10^9/L, or more than 10% band forms.

questions.pearl: SIRS needs 2 or more of 4 criteria; sepsis-3 now uses qSOFA: RR 22 or more, altered mentation, SBP 100 or less.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.text: It occurs mostly in old age
options.explanation: Usually over 50 years; in young patients consider multiple sclerosis.

options.label: B
options.text: It is caused by compression of the trigeminal nerve root
options.explanation: A tortuous vessel (often the superior cerebellar artery) compresses the root entry zone.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Carbamazepine is first-line drug treatment.

options.label: D
options.text: Gabapentin is needed to treat all patients
options.explanation: Gabapentin is only an alternative; many respond to carbamazepine, and refractory cases go for microvascular decompression.

questions.pearl: Trigeminal neuralgia: brief electric-shock pain in V2/V3 triggered by touch, chewing or washing.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Profuse bleeding during evacuation or spontaneous expulsion.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A late complication, developing weeks to months later in 2-3% of complete moles.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Infection of retained molar tissue is an immediate complication.

options.label: D
options.explanation: DIC can follow release of thromboplastin from molar tissue.

questions.pearl: Follow up moles with serial beta-hCG until normal; avoid pregnancy during follow-up.

questions.subject: Gynecology
questions.stem: Sites most commonly involved in endometriosis:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Endometrial tissue within the myometrium is adenomyosis, considered separately.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The ovary is the commonest site, forming chocolate cysts (endometriomas).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Tubal serosal involvement is common and causes adhesions and infertility.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pelvic peritoneum, pouch of Douglas and uterosacral ligaments are frequently involved.

questions.pearl: Endometriosis triad: dysmenorrhoea, dyspareunia, infertility; laparoscopy is the gold standard.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.text: It is a less common type
options.explanation: Viral (adenoviral) conjunctivitis is one of the commonest forms of conjunctivitis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Marked chemosis is uncommon; it is more typical of allergic or gonococcal conjunctivitis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Prominent itching suggests allergic conjunctivitis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Discharge is watery (serous); mucopurulent is bacterial, ropy mucoid is allergic.

questions.pearl: Viral conjunctivitis: watery discharge, follicles, tender preauricular node; highly contagious.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Cardinal features of primary open-angle glaucoma:

options.label: A
options.explanation: IOP is usually raised above 21 mmHg.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The optic disc shows glaucomatous cupping with increased cup-disc ratio.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Arcuate scotoma and peripheral field loss, sparing central vision until late.

options.label: D
options.text: Angle of anterior chamber is open
options.explanation: Gonioscopy shows an open angle, distinguishing it from angle-closure.

questions.pearl: POAG triad: raised IOP, optic disc cupping, field defects; first-line treatment is prostaglandin analogue drops.

questions.subject: Gynecology
questions.stem: Symptoms and signs of carcinoma cervix:

options.label: A
options.explanation: A late symptom from parametrial and nerve involvement.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Postcoital bleeding is the classic early symptom.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Offensive blood-stained discharge from the necrotic growth.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Dyspareunia can occur with an advanced or infected lesion.

questions.pearl: Ca cervix: HPV 16 and 18; commonest cause of death is uraemia from ureteric obstruction.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.stem: Maternal risk factors for abruptio placentae:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Abruption is more common in high parity.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Risk rises with maternal age, partly related to parity and hypertension.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Associated with malnutrition, smoking and poor antenatal care.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Trauma from ECV, especially under anaesthesia, is a recognised cause (Dutta).

questions.pearl: Hypertension (pre-eclampsia) is the commonest association of abruption; concealed type shows shock out of proportion to visible bleeding.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Genital tract infection is the most important cause.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Breast engorgement and mastitis cause fever in the puerperium.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Common after catheterisation in labour.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Wound infection is a recognised cause after CS.

questions.pearl: Puerperal pyrexia: 38 degrees C or more on two occasions 24 h apart within 10 days of delivery, excluding the first 24 h.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.stem: Causes of maternal death in eclampsia:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pulmonary capillary leak and aspiration can cause ARDS.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hypercoagulability and immobility increase thromboembolic risk.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Endothelial damage and HELLP may progress to DIC.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Severe hypertension and fluid overload precipitate pulmonary oedema.

questions.pearl: Commonest cause of death in eclampsia: cerebral haemorrhage. Drug of choice for fits: magnesium sulphate.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: The liver is tender from capsular stretch.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Visceral leishmaniasis causes painless hepatosplenomegaly.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Congestive hepatomegaly is tender because of rapid capsular distension.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Amoebic or pyogenic abscess causes a tender, painful liver.

questions.pearl: Painless hepatomegaly also: fatty liver, cirrhosis (early), lymphoma, leukaemia, metastases, storage diseases.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Infected nasal secretions reach the middle ear via the Eustachian tube, especially in children.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Obstruction of a sinus ostium, commonly frontoethmoidal, leads to mucocele.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Stage 1 of Chandler's orbital complications, usually from ethmoiditis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Frontal sinusitis can cause osteomyelitis of the frontal bone (Pott's puffy tumour).

questions.pearl: Chandler's orbital stages: preseptal cellulitis, orbital cellulitis, subperiosteal abscess, orbital abscess, cavernous sinus thrombosis.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Secreted by juxtaglomerular cells in response to low perfusion and sympathetic drive.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Red cells are produced in the bone marrow; the kidney only supplies the stimulus (erythropoietin).

options.label: C
options.explanation: 1-alpha-hydroxylase in the proximal tubule converts 25-OH D3 to 1,25-(OH)2 D3.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Produced by peritubular interstitial cells in response to hypoxia.

questions.pearl: CKD causes anaemia (low EPO) and renal osteodystrophy (low calcitriol); renin excess drives renovascular hypertension.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Bilateral nasal obstruction is caused by:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Ethmoidal polyps are usually multiple and bilateral, associated with allergy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Usually single and unilateral, arising from the maxillary sinus.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Blood collects on both sides of the septum, blocking both nostrils.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Bilateral septal swelling causes bilateral obstruction; risk of saddle nose.

questions.pearl: Unilateral nasal obstruction with blood-stained discharge in an adult: exclude malignancy; in a child, foreign body.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: A halogenated volatile agent widely used for maintenance.

options.label: B
options.explanation: An intravenous barbiturate induction agent.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A halogenated volatile agent; can provoke seizure activity on EEG.

options.label: D
options.explanation: An intravenous dissociative anaesthetic (NMDA antagonist).

questions.pearl: Sevoflurane is preferred for inhalational induction (non-pungent); desflurane gives fastest recovery but irritates airways.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery
questions.stem: Early features of raised intracranial pressure:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Typically worse in the morning and on coughing or straining.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Papilloedema is the sign; optic atrophy is a late consequence of chronic papilloedema.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Bradycardia with hypertension (Cushing reflex) is a late sign of impending herniation.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Not a feature of raised ICP; tachycardia in head injury suggests blood loss elsewhere.

questions.pearl: Early raised ICP: headache, vomiting, papilloedema. Late: Cushing triad of bradycardia, hypertension, irregular breathing.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: The Guedel oropharyngeal airway is a simple airway adjunct that only lifts the tongue off the posterior pharynx; it is not classed as a supraglottic airway device.

options.label: B
options.explanation: An endotracheal tube passes through the glottis into the trachea, making it an infraglottic (definitive) airway, not a supraglottic one.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The nasopharyngeal airway is a basic adjunct that bypasses nasal and tongue obstruction; it does not seal around the laryngeal inlet like a supraglottic device.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The LMA sits in the hypopharynx with its cuff sealing around the laryngeal inlet, above the vocal cords - the prototype supraglottic airway device.

questions.pearl: Supraglottic airway devices: LMA, i-gel, Baska mask, King laryngeal tube, Cobra perilaryngeal airway and the streamlined liner of the pharynx airway.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Causes of acute red eye are:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Rupture of a conjunctival vessel gives a sudden, painless, well-demarcated bright red patch; a common benign cause of red eye.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Corneal inflammation or infection causes a painful red eye with ciliary (circumcorneal) injection, photophobia and reduced vision.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Migraine causes headache and visual aura but not conjunctival injection; red eye with headache should prompt thinking of acute angle-closure glaucoma or cluster headache.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Acute angle-closure glaucoma gives a painful red eye, hazy cornea, mid-dilated fixed pupil and very high intraocular pressure; an ophthalmic emergency.

questions.pearl: Painful red eye with reduced vision (keratitis, iritis, acute glaucoma) needs urgent referral; conjunctivitis and subconjunctival haemorrhage spare vision.
